The atom

Series H: the electron circling the proton with its momentum arrow and its copies spreading, its phase turning by its momentum.

A registered world, examples/events/bohr/r8.json, run as it is declared; its register entry is H, Bohr's lines behind the detector (2026-09-20). Nothing was changed in the world and nothing is pinned by this page.

The GameBoard

An open cube of 45 x 45 x 45 Nodes, K = 1 073 741 824, N = 64, the world's action h = 5 414 584 320 (the identity bohr-v1). The proton at (22, 22, 22), measured event 1: a fixed body of 1836 units of p (charge [1, 1]) releasing one row per direction of a shell of 2616 primitive directions every 10 intervals, its field. The electron, measured event 2: a free body of 1836 units of e (charge -15, a phase circle) on a set of three Nodes (span [1, 1, 3]) at r = 8 on the +x axis, with the tangential momentum p = (0, 338411520, 0) the series README derives from the engine's own flight lines for a circular orbit, turning its phase by its momentum at every Link it steps (phase_by_momentum under h) and releasing rows on four directions that carry that phase to the open faces, the wave detectors of what comes out of the atom.

the p rowsthe e rows, coloured by their phasethe proton (a body of p)the electron (a body of e), coloured by its phase

Why this page

The owner asked that a body be shown with its spreading: "if one sees an electron, one should also see its spreading, its copies in space, transparent, and the arrow of its vector, where it travels". Here the electron is that body: at every self-creation it releases rows on its directions (its copies, the translucent discs that spread from it at the pace of the flight table), it reads the proton's rows and is pushed by the one coupling (the charge column), its momentum vector p is the white arrow, and its phase, an element of Z_64, turns by |p| N over h at every Link it steps, so the disc's colour goes round the circle as it orbits. What a detector reads of the atom is on the faces: the coherent record of the electron's rows.

The moving picture

What to see: the electron circles the proton, its arrow turning with it and its copies streaming outward; the proton's shell of copies pulses every 10 intervals through the plane; the phase colour of the electron turns as it moves. The register (the signed-drive re-read of series H, then the turn by momentum as a row of the counts table): the orbit at r = 8 closes the angle twice (T 1292, 2016), the phase's turn per orbit 0.969 against the expected 0, the faces' coherence C(2) = 1.24, and the electron leaves at 3869; Bohr's lines are not read and the register keeps that verdict, nothing tuned. In this run the electron left through face:+y at the interval 3869.
